cardiovascular-service-framework-england.name: Heart disease and stroke framework for England
cardiovascular-service-framework-england.headline: Government and NHS England publish a 10-year framework on heart disease and stroke
cardiovascular-service-framework-england.summary: The government and NHS England have published a cardiovascular disease framework that aims to cut premature deaths from heart disease and stroke by a quarter within a decade.
keyPoints: The Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England published a cardiovascular disease modern service framework on 7 July 2026.
It sets a 10-year aim of cutting premature deaths from heart disease and stroke in England by a quarter.
The government describes 12 priorities for the first three years.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The government and NHS England say the framework is a 10-year strategic vision to reduce premature deaths from heart disease and stroke in England. It sets out 12 priorities for the next three years. The government says the priorities include finding people at risk of cardiovascular disease, blood pressure and cholesterol treatment targets, stroke care and rehabilitation. It also includes a partnership with Diabetes UK to raise public awareness of the link between type 2 diabetes and heart disease.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The government estimates that successful implementation could prevent between 1,600 and 2,400 premature deaths a year from heart disease and stroke in people under 75 in the first three years. It estimates this would rise to between 3,850 and 4,900 deaths a year after a decade. These are the government's projections, not results already achieved. The government describes the framework as part of a shift from reactive care towards prevention.

flu-jab-booking-opens-winter-2026.name: NHS opens booking for winter 2026 flu jab
flu-jab-booking-opens-winter-2026.headline: NHS England urges eligible people to book a flu jab before winter
flu-jab-booking-opens-winter-2026.summary: NHS England says national booking for this winter's flu jab is open, with children and pregnant women vaccinated from 1 September and other groups from 1 October.
keyPoints: NHS England said on 17 August 2026 that the national booking system for this winter's flu jab was open.
Children and pregnant women are in the first group, with vaccinations starting on 1 September.
Other groups start on 1 October, including people aged 65 and over and adults in a clinical risk group.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NHS England says the national booking system is open for this winter's flu jab. Children and pregnant women form the first group, and their vaccinations start on 1 September. Other groups start on 1 October. These include people aged 65 and over, adults in a clinical risk group, carers, people in close contact with someone who has a weakened immune system, and frontline healthcare workers.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The announcement says the jab can be pre-booked at a community pharmacy. It says local services will begin sending invitations through GP practices, the NHS App or by letter. Dr Julie Yates of the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) urged eligible people to plan ahead and book as soon as possible now that the national booking system is open.

flu-vaccinations-ten-million-october-202.name: Over 10 million flu jabs delivered in England
flu-vaccinations-ten-million-october-202.headline: Government says more than 10 million flu vaccinations delivered as winter campaign runs on social media
flu-vaccinations-ten-million-october-202.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care says more than 10 million flu vaccinations have been delivered in England, and a social media campaign now includes TikTok.
keyPoints: On 22 October 2026 the Department of Health and Social Care said more than 10 million flu vaccinations had been delivered since bookings opened in August.
The figure includes 2.7 million vaccinations in the week of the announcement.
The government's social media campaign runs on Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat and, for the first time, TikTok.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The Department of Health and Social Care says more than 10 million flu vaccinations have been delivered in England since bookings first opened in August and vaccinations began in September. This includes 2.7 million vaccinations in that week. The government is running a social media campaign on Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat and, for the first time, TikTok. It is also promoting an NHS App feature that lets people check their eligibility and book a flu jab at a community pharmacy.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The release cites UKHSA modelling estimating flu vaccination prevented around 100,000 hospitalisations and 7,000 deaths in England last season.

mirvetuximab-ovarian-cancer-nhs-rollout.name: NHS rolls out new ovarian cancer drug
mirvetuximab-ovarian-cancer-nhs-rollout.headline: NHS England begins offering mirvetuximab soravtansine for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
mirvetuximab-ovarian-cancer-nhs-rollout.summary: NHS England has begun offering mirvetuximab soravtansine to hundreds of women with ovarian cancer that has stopped responding to platinum-based chemotherapy.
keyPoints: NHS England announced on 4 June 2026 that mirvetuximab soravtansine would be available on the NHS from that day.
It follows a recommendation by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE).
NHS England describes it as the first new addition to NHS treatment for this type of cancer in over 20 years.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NHS England says hundreds of women with hard-to-treat ovarian cancer can have mirvetuximab soravtansine on the NHS from 4 June 2026. Following the NICE recommendation, it is for epithelial ovarian, peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer that has become resistant to platinum-based chemotherapy and whose tumours contain the folate receptor alpha (FR alpha) protein that the drug targets.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The drug combines a homing antibody with a cancer-killing medicine. NHS England says it may have more tolerable side effects than traditional chemotherapy.

source.title: NHS rolls out life-extending drug for hundreds of women with ovarian cancer
